factor.argument: Independent review of held patch e1b2dba5 (base 6e7c2a3c; landed as ce40a647 while I reviewed — operator-approved 01:01:52Z over codex's dissent). GT plane verified CLEAN: hooks_gt.check on the worktree shows zero #1411 findings (committed core digests to the manifest's c05eefac under the canonical header-zeroing rule), all five manifests' gt_version recompute exactly, applied tree is byte-identical to the held patch's post-image, and the applied gate-core suite passes. Feature shape verified behaviorally: a read of a nonexistent path denies as mrh.path.nonexistent and opens no scope request; existing out-of-scope reads and any write keep the ordinary mrh.path path. DISSENT, seconding codex with independent reproduction (in-memory exec of the applied module, synthetic fixtures): _did_you_mean checks os.path.lexists only and never grant coverage. (1) Under an exact path:<root> grant, a read of <ws>/hestia/<base>/child.txt draws 'did you mean <root>/child.txt — inside your grant path:<root>' while _within_path_grant is False and the follow-up read denies mrh.path: false authorization guidance. (2) Under a recursive grant, a symlink escaping the root draws the hint for <root>/link/note.txt though realpath containment fails: the hint probes and discloses existence beyond the member's grants. Narrow trigger (the grant root's basename must appear as a path segment), no access bypass — the read stays denied — so this is a follow-up repair, not a revert: validate the candidate with the gate's own coverage test (exact/recursive + realpath containment) before the lexists/hint, and add exact-grant-descendant and escaping-symlink regression tests.
